source.quote: SMSL's own page for the SU-10, read 2026-11-24: « ES9038PRO D/A chips from ESS, and using all 16 channels, up to 21 OPA1612A operational amplifiers in total »; « Use USB XMOS XU-316, a 32-bit USB scheme, which supports DoP and native DSD, with PCM up to 768kHz and DSD up to DSD512 »; « USB, Optical, Coaxial, I2S, AES support DSD, Coaxial , Optical and AES support DOP64 ».

facts.chip: ES9038PRO (ESS) « using all 16 channels », with an XMOS XU-316 as the USB interface. The channel count is the maker's own and is exactly the case classes.json flags: a device paralleling all of a chip's channels is arguably multi-element, where the ess_sabre family assumes single.

_five_inputs_split_by_transport: « USB, Optical, Coaxial, I2S, AES support DSD, Coaxial , Optical and AES support DOP64 » splits five inputs in one sentence: all five take DSD, three take it as DoP64, so USB and I2S are the native ones. Richest per-input DSD statement in this catalogue. No PCM ceiling is recorded for the four non-USB inputs: the 768 kHz figure belongs to the XMOS sentence, which is about USB.
